 DEFENDANT'S CHALLENGE TO ENTIRE PANEL OF
 PROSPECTIVE TRIAL JURORS

The defendant moves to strike the entire panel of prospective trial jurors because highly prejudicial
statements were made and heard by the panel and it cannot be cured.

The Massachusetts Superior Court [OPTIONAL LANGUAGE: and District Court] rules allow for juror venire
by the parties. The Superior Court Rule 6(3)(e) prohibits parties from asking certain types of questions.
Specifically, the Rule prohibits:

 • Questions framed in terms of how the juror would decide this case (prejudgment), including
 hypotheticals that are close/specific to the facts of this case (any hypotheticals that may trigger this rule
 must be presented to the judge before trial)

 • Questions that seek to commit juror(s) to a result, including, without limitation, questions about what
 evidence would cause the juror(s) to find for the attorney's client or the party

 • Questions having no substantial purpose other than to argue an attorney's or party's case or
 indoctrinate any juror(s)

And, here, the prosecutor during the venire asked the following improper question(s):

 [Specify question(s) asked]. This caused prejudice to the defendant requiring the dismissal of the entire
 panel and declaring a mistrial. ALM R. Crim. P. Rule 20(a).

COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS

 [COURT NAME] OF THE TRIAL COURT

 [COUNTY] COUNTY, SS.

COMMONWEALTH; )

 )

[defendant name] )

 )

Defendant. )

 Motion for Change of Venue (Criminal) (MA)

NOW COMES the Defendant, by and through counsel, and hereby moves this Court, pursuant to
Massachusetts Rule of Criminal Procedure 37(b)(1), to transfer this proceeding to another county because
there exists in [county] County, the County of prosecution, so great a prejudice against the Defendant that
[he/she/they] cannot obtain a fair and impartial trial. In support of this Motion the Defendant shows unto the
Court as follows:
 1.

 The Defendant believes that it is reasonably likely that prospective jurors would base their decision in this
 case upon pretrial information and publications rather than the evidence presented at trial and would be
 unable to remove from their minds any preconceived feelings and impressions that they might have formed.
 2.

 Such pretrial information that would unduly prejudice the Defendant has been presented in the form of print
 and electronic media coverage of matters that may not be relevant to or admissible at trial and which have
 so polluted the prospective jury pool to make it reasonably likely that potential jurors would base their
 decision in this matter on pretrial information and feelings rather than the evidence presented at trial.
 3.

 Furthermore, the Defendant submits that a trial held in [county] County would violate [his/her/their] right to
 a fair and impartial trial under both the United States and Massachusetts Constitutions in that the [name of
 publication/publications] published [type of information (e.g., an interview of the Defendant in which
 [he/she/they] admitted to…")].
 4.

 This publicity has resulted in a substantial amount of prejudice among the jury pool against the Defendant
 and a change of venue is required to guarantee the Defendant's right to due process of law.

WHEREFORE, the Defendant moves for the proceedings in this case to be transferred to another county to
ensure [he/she/they] receive a fair and impartial trial.

 Motion for Change of Venue (Criminal) (MA)

Respectfully submitted,
____________________

 Motion for Complete Recordation of Trial Proceedings (Criminal) (MA)

NOW COMES the Defendant by and through counsel and moves this Court for an Order allowing that the trial
of this matter and any related hearings be recorded and transcribed. In support of this motion the Defendant
shows unto the Court as follows.
 1.

 Pursuant to pursuant to Massachusetts General Law Chapter 221, Section 91(B), defendants can have a
 stenographer record any hearing or proceeding in connection with a criminal case in which a court-
 appointed stenographer is not present. In this case, a court-appointed stenographer has not been assigned,
 and the proceedings are to be recorded by an electronic recording system.
 2.

 Pursuant to the Sixth Amendment of the United States Constitution, a defendant is entitled to confront and
 cross-examine all witnesses against them, including, under effective cross-examination, the right to
 impeach or confront a witness with prior statements.
 3.

 The charge in this case relates directly to a felony charge of [identify felony charge(s) the Defendant is
 facing (e.g., possession of a handgun by a felon now pending against the Defendant)] and as such the
 testimony of the officers involved in any pretrial hearings will be relevant to an effective defense in this
 case.

Wherefore, the Defendant requests that this Court enter an Order allowing all proceedings relating to this
proceeding be recorded and thereafter transcribed by a stenographer obtained at the Defendant's expense.

 Motion for Complete Recordation of Trial Proceedings (Criminal) (MA)

 Motion for Continuance (Criminal) (MA)

 [FIRST] [UNOPPOSED] MOTION FOR CONTINUANCE OF TRIAL

COMES NOW the defendant, [name of defendant], and files this Motion for Continuance of trial date and shows
the Court the following:
 1.

 Defendant was [indicted] [charged] on [month] [day], [year], just [number of days (e.g., twelve (12))] days
 ago and defense counsel was only recently retained to represent defendant in this matter.
 2.

 Defense counsel is successor counsel and was just retained by the defendant on [date of retention]. They
 need time to prepare defense motions in this case, which may require pretrial hearings and rulings by the
 court. This case is [unusual or complex] because of [reason] and "it is unreasonable to expect adequate
 preparation of the case at the time it is scheduled for trial . . . ." Mass Rules of Criminal Procedure, Rule
 10(a)(2)(B). Moreover, defense counsel understands that the Commonwealth intends to supplement its
 discovery significantly, but has not done so yet, and any information disclosed to this defendant will require
 ample time for investigation prior to trial.
 3.

 Additional time is needed to interview witnesses, prepare requests to charge and investigate the
 circumstances of this case.
 4.

 The defendant is guaranteed a right to effective counsel by the Sixth and Fourteenth Amendments to the
 United States Constitution and by Article 12 of the Massachusetts Constitution and M.G.L. c. 263, § 5.
 5.

 Counsel would not be prepared to render effective representation if the case proceeds to trial as now
 scheduled.
 6.

 [Any additional reasons why the court should continue the trial (e.g., defense counsel is scheduled to
 appear in another case which will take time to present)]
 7.

 The Commonwealth [opposes / does not oppose] this motion.

 Motion for Continuance (Criminal) (MA)

WHEREFORE, defendant moves the Court to continue the trial of this case to a later date pursuant to Rule 10
of the Rules of Criminal Procedure as it is in the "interest of justice" to do so.

 Motion for Judgment of Acquittal at the Close of All the Evidence (MA)

 RENEWED MOTION FOR REQUIRED FINDING OF NOT GUILTY

Defendant, [name of defendant], by counsel, moves this Court, pursuant to Mass. R. Crim. P. 25(b)(2), for
required findings of not guilty on the grounds that the evidence presented is insufficient as a matter of law
to sustain a conviction of any of the charges. The reasons for this request include:
 1.

 The evidence failed to establish the corpus delicti, i.e.: that the offense charged was in fact committed.
 Commonwealth v. Leonard, 401 Mass. 470, 473 (1988) (setting aside conviction because of lack of
 evidence); Commonwealth v. Salemme, 395 Mass. 594, 601 (1985) ("Evidence which does not go
 beyond showing that the defendant had an opportunity to commit the crime is insufficient.");
 Commonwealth v. Acosta, 81 Mass. App. Ct. 836, 844, 969 N.E.2d 720, 726 (2012) (setting aside
 verdict because of lack of evidence regarding essential element of offense). The Commonwealth failed
 to present any evidence regarding the third element, which required [details on evidence for third
 element].

 Motion for Judgment of Acquittal at the Close of All the Evidence (MA)

WHEREFORE, defendant prays for a required finding of not guilty and that [he/she/they] be discharged.

[Date]

 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS

 [County], ss. [court name]

 OF THE TRIAL COURT

COMMONWEALTH; )

 )

[name of defendant] )

 )

 Defendant. )

 Motion for a Required Finding of Not Guilty, and Objection to Instructions (MA)

 MOTION FOR REQUIRED FINDING OF NOT GUILTY

Defendant, [name of defendant], by counsel, moves this Court, pursuant to Mass. R. Crim. P. 25, for
required findings of not guilty on the grounds that the evidence presented is insufficient as a matter of law
to sustain a conviction of any of the charges. The reasons for this request include:
 1.

 There was no evidence introduced into the trial to establish the essential elements of the charged
 offense, [charged offense]. There was no evidence introduced into the trial to prove [elements of the
 charged offense] as required by [statute]. Under this state of the evidence, the due process clause of
 the fourteenth amendment of the United States Constitution requires a directed verdict of acquittal on
 all counts. Commonwealth v. Leonard, 401 Mass. 470, 473 (1988) (setting aside conviction because of
 lack of evidence); Commonwealth v. Salemme, 395 Mass. 594, 601 (1985) ("Evidence which does not
 go beyond showing that the defendant had an opportunity to commit the crime is insufficient.");
 Commonwealth v. Acosta, 81 Mass. App. Ct. 836, 844, 969 N.E.2d 720, 726 (2012) (setting aside
 verdict because of lack of evidence regarding essential element of offense).
 2.

 Even if the evidence introduced into the trial proves [met element(s) of a charged offense (e.g., that the
 defendant negligently caused the deaths of the victims)], such evidence does not permit a criminal
 conviction. Commonwealth v. Life Care Centers of Am., Inc., 456 Mass. 826, 836, 926 N.E.2d 206, 214
 (2010) (negligence is insufficient for a conviction).
 3.

 Defendant objects to the Court instructing on [charged offense] since there is no evidence, or in the
 alternative, since there is insufficient evidence that [elements of offense that were not met (e.g.,
 defendant wantonly caused the deaths of the victims)].

 Motion for a Required Finding of Not Guilty, and Objection to Instructions (MA)

WHEREFORE, defendant moves for a required finding of not guilty on all counts, and objects to the Court
instructing on [charged offense].
Respectfully submitted,
____________________
[name of attorney for defendant], [BBO #]

 Motion to Reveal Witness Identity (Criminal) (MA)

NOW COMES the Defendant, by and through counsel, and moves this Court for an Order requiring the
Commonwealth to provide the name and contact information of the confidential informant listed as a witness
and exchange facilitator in the reports of Detective [detective name]. In support of this Motion the Defendant
shows unto the Court as follows:
 1.

 The Defendant is currently charged with [identify offense(s), (e.g., possession with sale and delivery of
 Clonazepam and PWISD Clonazepam)].
 2.

 An alleged transaction in this matter occurred between the Defendant and Detective [detective name] in
 the presence of the confidential informant on [month] [day], [year], which the Commonwealth now intends to
 offer as evidence linking the Defendant to [description of offense, (e.g., possession and control of this
 controlled substance)].
 3.

 According to the Commonwealth's discovery file, this confidential informant arranged the transaction and
 was present as it was conducted with the Detective.
 4.

 The entire sale and bargaining for said sale was conducted between the Detective and the Defendant in
 the presence of the confidential informant.
 5.

 Counsel for the Defendant needs the name and contact information of this witness, all police department
 files regarding the confidential informant's contact with the Defendant, and the remuneration arrangements
 for the confidential informant, to adequately prepare the Defendant's case for trial. This information is
 especially necessary for the Defendant's counsel to explore and develop any impeachment material as it
 relates to the testimony of Detective [detective name] regarding this transaction.

WHEREFORE, the Defendant moves this Court for an order requiring the Commonwealth to reveal the name of
the confidential informant who arranged the transaction at issue and implicates the Defendant and for such
other and further relief to which the Defendant may be entitled and which the Court may deem just and proper.

 Motion to Reveal Witness Identity (Criminal) (MA)

Respectfully submitted,

Affidavit in Support of Application to Suppress Evidence Seized Pursuant to
 Search Warrant
 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS

 Affidavit in Support of Application to Suppress Evidence Seized Pursuant to Search Warrant (MA)

[COUNTY], ss. [COURT NAME]

 OF THE TRIAL COURT

COMMONWEALTH; )

 )

 )

v. ) Docket No. [number]

 )

[defendant name] )

 )

Defendant. )

 Affidavit in Support of Application to Suppress Evidence Seized Pursuant to Search Warrant (MA)

[Defendant attorney name], an attorney admitted to practice in the courts of the Commonwealth of
Massachusetts, hereby affirms the following under penalty of perjury:
 1.

 I am familiar with the facts and proceedings herein. I make this affirmation in support of the Defendant's
 Motion to Suppress [identify item(s) evidence to be suppressed].
 2.

 The Defendant was indicted on [month] [day], [year], and was charged with the [crime/crimes] of [list
 crime(s)].
 3.

 The Defendant entered a plea of not guilty to the indictment on [month] [day], [year], and the case has
 been scheduled for trial on [month] [day], [year].
 4.

 On [month] [day], [year], [executing officer name] executed a search warrant of the Defendant's
 [residence/vehicle/person] and seized [item(s) of property seized during search].
 5.

 The evidence seized during this search should be suppressed because the search was conducted in
 violation of the Defendant's constitutional rights as the warrant was not supported by probable cause.
 6.

 "The fundamental principle under both the Fourth Amendment to the United States Constitution and art. 14
 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights has been that no search or seizure is to be deemed
 "reasonable" unless based on a warrant issued on probable cause." Commonwealth v. Shields, 402 Mass.
 162, 169, 521 N.E.2d 987, 992 (1988).
 7.

 In this case, the warrant used to search the Defendant's [residence/vehicle/person] was not based on an
 affidavit with sufficient probable cause. Specifically, the affidavit did not establish a reasonable belief that
 evidence of the crime alleged would be found [at/in/on] the [residence/vehicle/person], which was the
 specified location in the search warrant application.

WHEREFORE, the affiant respectfully requests that the Defendant's Motion to Suppress the above-identified
evidence be granted and for such further relief to which the Defendant may be entitled.

 Affidavit in Support of Application to Suppress Evidence Seized Pursuant to Search Warrant (MA)

Date: ____________________
Respectfully submitted,
____________________
(Signature of Defendant's attorney)
[defendant attorney name], Attorney for Defendant
[Office Street Address]
[OPTIONAL: P.O. Box address]

 Motion to Compel Discovery of Exculpatory Evidence (MA)

The Defendant, by and through counsel, moves this court pursuant to Brady v. Maryland, 373 U.S. 83 (1963)
and under the Sixth, Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments to the United States Constitution to order the
Commonwealth to turn over to defense counsel any materials in the possession of the Commonwealth and law
enforcement agencies which are favorable to the Defendant, including, but not limited to the following:
 1.

 Any statement of any witness or from any source, exculpating the Defendant or otherwise indicating a
 lessened role of the Defendant in this case by any government agency.
 2.

 Any exculpatory statements made by, or attributed to, the Defendant.
 3.

 Any statements of any witnesses or from any sources indicating that the Defendant did not act with
 premeditation or deliberation or which indicate that the Defendant did not act with the specific intent to kill.
 4.

 Any reports or evidence of threats, deals, arrangements, promises, or inducements made to any
 prosecution witness in this case.
 5.

 The criminal records of all prosecution witnesses including prior convictions and cases pending at the
 present time or at the time of the Defendant's arrest.
 6.

 Any evidence of law enforcement officers making monetary payments to, or promises of monetary
 payments to, any material witness or informant in this case.
 7.

 Any alias or other names used by any prosecution witness.
 8.

 Any evidence of any mental or emotional illness, or drug or alcohol use by, any of the prosecution
 witnesses at the time of this offense or any time thereafter.
 9.

 Any evidence of any out of court statements by any prosecution witness which differs from the witness
 testimony which is expected to be given at the upcoming trial.
 10.

 The names and addresses of any individuals who were considered at any time during the case as possible
 suspects and the evidence that led to this conclusion.
 11.

 Any evidence that another person other than the accused was in possession of the alleged murder
 weapon.
 12.

 Motion to Compel Discovery of Exculpatory Evidence (MA)

 Any evidence that another person other than the accused attempted to dispose of the alleged murder
 weapon after the time of this alleged offense.
 13.

 A list of any evidence that has been destroyed by law enforcement authorities in this case and the policy
 that allowed such destruction.
 14.

 Any evidence or information that indicates that evidence was obtained in violation of the Massachusetts or
 the Federal Constitution.

Wherefore, the Defendant requests that this Court order that the State provide all such materials within the
possession of the State immediately and all such materials no later than two months prior to the start of trial to
allow [him/her/them] to adequately investigate such evidence and effectively utilize it in [his/her/their] defense.

 MOTION TO QUASH GRAND JURY SUBPOENA

COMES NOW [name(s) of movants], Movants, through their attorney(s) of record, [name(s) of attorney(s)
for defendant/witness], and request this Court to quash grand jury subpoenas issued to Movants. In support
of this motion, Movants would show the Court the following:
 1.

 The subpoenas for Movants to appear before the grand jury have not been issued in accordance with
 the statutory requirements of [statutory authority].
 2.

 [name of movant] and the other Movants are potential defendants, and they may invoke the Fifth
 Amendment privilege not to testify. "Grand juries 'may not override constitutional rights, such as the
 right against self-incrimination.'" In re Grand Jury Subpoena, 454 Mass. 685, 692, 912 N.E.2d 970, 976
 (2009) (quoting Powers v. Commonwealth, 387 Mass. 563, 564–565 (1982)).
 3.

 The subpoenas make unreasonable requests for records. Grand jury subpoenas "may not issue
 unreasonable orders to produce documents." In re Grand Jury Subpoena, 454 Mass. 685, 692, 912
 N.E.2d 970, 976 (2009) (citing Commonwealth v. Doe,408 Mass. 764, 768, 563 N.E.2d 1349 (1990)).
 This request is vague and potentially covers hundreds of thousands of documents. It will take dozens of
 employees hundreds of hours to produce such documents and Movants have not received any
 information that indicates that any will be relevant to any investigation.
 4.

 It is an abuse of the grand jury function to use the grand jury for the purpose of gaining evidence
 where a criminal complaint or indictment has been presented.
 5.

 [Number] persons, [number] of whom [is/are] [a Movant/Movants], presently stand charged with
 [description of offense]. It is an abuse of the grand jury process to use this grand jury in an attempt to
 gain further evidence for use in these pending criminal actions.

 Motion to Quash Grand Jury Subpoenas (MA)

WHEREFORE, PREMISES CONSIDERED, Movants request that this Court grant this motion and order the
subpoenas in this cause quashed.

 MEMORANDUM OF LAW IN SUPPORT OF MOTION TO SUPPRESS STATEMENTS
 Pursuant to Rule 13 of the Massachusetts Rules of Criminal Procedure, the Defendant moves for an
order suppressing any statements allegedly made by the defendant on [date] to [agents/officers] of the
[name of the law enforcement agency], to be offered in evidence at trial.
FACTS
 [Set forth the relevant facts of the case. Incorporate affidavit.]
ARGUMENT
 The police are required to inform individuals of Miranda rights prior to questioning them after
 placing them under arrest. Any statement Defendant allegedly made to the police while in custody
 prior to receiving their Miranda rights violated the Defendant's rights under the 4th Amendment to
 United States Constitution, Article 14 and Article 12 of the Massachusetts Declaration of Rights as
 well as Commonwealth v. Canavan, 40 Mass. App. Ct. 642 (1996); Commonwealth v. Lubiejewski,
 49 Mass. App. Ct. 212, 214 (2000). The police arrested the Defendant, placed [him/her/them] in
 custody, and questioned [him/her/them] without providing Miranda rights. As such, the statements
 of the Defendant should be excluded from trial as they were obtained in violation of the Defendant's
 constitutional rights. United States Constitution, Amendment 4; Article 14 and Article 12 of the
 Massachusetts Declaration of Rights; Commonwealth v. Lubiejewski, 49 Mass. App. Ct. 212, 214
 (2000).
 For the reasons set forth herein, the Court should allow Defendant's motion to suppress
 statements.

Notice of Motion for Discovery Where the Prosecution Has Refused to Comply with A Demand to Produce (MA)

 MOTION FOR SANCTIONS FOR THE COMMONWEALTH'S FAILURE TO FULFILL ITS DISCOVERY
 OBLIGATIONS

 The Defendant moves for an order for sanctions for the failure of the Commonwealth to fulfill its discovery
 obligations. Specifically, the Commonwealth failed to disclose [specify missing item(s)].
 FACTS
 1.

 The Defendant is charged with [name of criminal offense(s)].
 2.

 The [police report / grand jury minutes] references a 911 call from the Commonwealth's principal
 witness, [principal witness name]. [Provide cite in the record the reference.]
 3.

 The Commonwealth agreed to produce [evidence the Commonwealth agreed to produce] in the
 pretrial conference report the Defendant and Commonwealth filed at the arraignment on [month]
 [day], [year], as well as in response to the Defendant's demand for discovery. Despite this
 commitment, the Commonwealth did not disclose such evidence on the pretrial conference date, as
 agreed, on [month] [day], [year] [OPTIONAL LANGUAGE: or on the subsequent continuation of
 the pretrial conference on [month] [day], [year] and [month] [day], [year]].
 ARGUMENT

 The Commonwealth was required pursuant to ALM R. Crim. P. Rule 14(a)(1)(A) to make
 mandatory disclosures to the defendant. In addition, the Commonwealth specifically committed in
 the pretrial conference filed on [month] [day]. [year], to produce [evidence not produced]. The
 Commonwealth has not produced [evidence not produced], which could provide critical evidence
 for the defense.

 "When a party violates its discovery obligations, the trial judge may issue a sanction."
 Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. 1, 8 (2022) (ALM R. Crim. P. Rule 14(c)). "Sanctions for
 discovery violations are 'a mechanism for protecting a defendant's right to a fair trial' by ensuring
 that the Commonwealth complies with its discovery obligations." Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491
 Mass. at 8 (quoting Commonwealth v. Frith, 458 Mass. 434, 439 (2010)).

 The Court has broad discretion to impose a sanction. "[T]he court may make a further order for
 discovery, grant a continuance, or enter such other order as it deems just under the
 circumstances." Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. at 8, 198 (quoting ALM R. Crim. P. Rule
 14(c)(1). The Court may also exclude evidence or dismiss the case for the Commonwealth's
 failures. Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. at 8 (citing ALM R. Crim. P. Rule 14(c)(1) and (2)).

 When deciding what sanction is appropriate, "[f]irst, sanctions are remedial in nature. Second,
 sanctions should be tailored appropriately to cure any prejudice resulting from a party's
 noncompliance and to ensure a fair trial." Sanford, 460 Mass. 441, 445-446 (2011).

 A dismissal with prejudice is warranted "where there is egregious prosecutorial or police
 misconduct and prejudice to the defendant's right to a fair trial, and where the dismissal is
 necessary to cure the prejudice." Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. at 9 (quoting
 Commonwealth v. Washington W., 462 Mass. 204, 215, 967 N.E.2d 615 (2012); ALM R. Crim. P.
 Rule 14(c)(1)). Here, the prosecutor appears to have hidden [evidence not disclosed], it refuses to
 confirm or deny it, and it is depriving the Defendant of a key line of cross-examination at trial. The

Notice of Motion for Discovery Where the Prosecution Has Refused to Comply with A Demand to Produce (MA)

 defendant is highly prejudiced by this misconduct, justifying dismissal. Commonwealth v. Mason,
 453 Mass. 873, 877 (2009).

 For the reasons set forth herein, the Court should allow defendant's motion for sanctions should be
 allowed.

 Respectfully submitted,
 ____________________
 (Signature of Defendant's attorney)

MOTION FOR SANCTIONS UNDER RULE 14(c) FOR THE COMMONWEALTH'S FAILURE TO MAKE
 MANDATORY DISCLOSURES

Pursuant to Rule 14(c) of the Massachusetts Rules of Criminal Procedure, the defendant moves for an
order for sanctions for the failure of the of Commonwealth to make its mandatory disclosures under Rule
14(a)(1)(A). Specifically, the Commonwealth failed to disclose [specify missing item(s)].

 FACTS

 The defendant is charged with [name of criminal offense(s)].
 2.

 The [police report / grand jury minutes] references [undisclosed evidence]. [Provide cite in the record
 for reference].

 The Commonwealth agreed to produce [specify undisclosed evidence] referenced in [specify source of
 the evidence] in the pretrial conference report the defendant and Commonwealth filed at the
 arraignment on [month] [day], [year]. Despite this commitment, the Commonwealth did not disclose
 [specify undisclosed evidence] on the pretrial conference date, as agreed, on [month] [day],
 [year][OPTIONAL LANGUAGE: or on the subsequent continuation of the pretrial conference on
 [month] [day], [year] and [month] [day], [year]].

 ARGUMENT

 The Commonwealth was required pursuant to Mass. R. Crim. P. 14(a)(1)(A) to make mandatory
 disclosures to the defendant. In addition, the Commonwealth specifically committed in the pretrial
 conference filed on [date] to produce [evidence not produced.] The Commonwealth has not produced
 [evidence not produced], which could provide critical evidence for the defense.

 "When a party violates its discovery obligations, the trial judge may issue a sanction." Commonwealth
 v. Edwards, 491 Mass. 1, 8 (2022) (Mass. R. Crim. P. 14 (c)). "Sanctions for discovery violations are 'a
 mechanism for protecting a defendant's right to a fair trial' by ensuring that the Commonwealth
 complies with its discovery obligations." Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. at 8 (quoting
 Commonwealth v. Frith, 458 Mass. 434, 439 (2010)).

 The Court has broad discretion to impose a sanction. "[T]he court may make a further order for
 discovery, grant a continuance, or enter such other order as it deems just under the circumstances."
 Commonwealth v. Edwards, 491 Mass. at 8, 198 (quoting Mass. R. Crim. P. 14 (c) (1). The Court may
 also exclude evidence or dismiss the case for the Commonwealth's failures. Commonwealth v.
 Edwards, 491 Mass. at 8 (citing Mass. R. Crim. P. 14 (c)(1) and (2)).

 When deciding what sanction is appropriate, "[f]irst, sanctions are remedial in nature. Second,
 sanctions should be tailored appropriately to cure any prejudice resulting from a party's noncompliance
 and to ensure a fair trial." Sanford, 460 Mass. 441 445-446 (2011).

 Trial is scheduled on [month] [day], [year]. The defendant deserves to have their day in Court and end
 a resolution of this matter as soon as possible. No more delays by the Commonwealth should be
 permitted. The Commonwealth has failed to make these mandatory disclosures, which the defendant
 specifically requested on [month] [day], [year][OPTIONAL LANGUAGE: and [month] [day], [year]]. The
 Court has broad discretion to exclude evidence and it should exclude reference to [specify undisclosed
 evidence]. Mass. R. Crim. P. 14 (c) (2).

 Application to Modify Bail (MA)

 MOTION FOR MODIFICATION OF BAIL ORDER

Defendant [name of defendant] makes this motion to [modify their conditions of release/lower their bail]:
 1.

 Defendant has been arrested in [location] and charged with the offense of [offense], which offense
 allegedly took place in [county where offense took place] County, [state] on or about [month] [day],
 [year].
 2.

 Defendant was arraigned in Court on [date] and [bail was set at $x/the following conditions of release
 were set: [release conditions]]
 3.

 Since the arraignment, Defendant has lost their income as a result of the incarceration. Defendant
 lived paycheck to paycheck prior to incarceration and has no savings. See attached Affidavit.
 4.

 Defendant cannot afford to pay the bail set and, as a result, SJC precedent requires modifying the bail.
 Brangan v. Commonwealth, 477 Mass. 691, 693 (2017) ("we conclude that in setting the amount of
 bail, whether under G.L.c. 276, § 57 or § 58, a judge must consider a defendant's financial resources,
 but is not required to set bail in an amount Defendant can afford if other relevant considerations weigh
 more heavily than Defendant's ability to provide the necessary security for their appearance at trial.").
 5.

 In addition, Defendant has lived their whole life in [location], is married with [number] children who
 reside with Defendant in [location], and has extended family, including their mother, father, and
 [number] siblings and their families, who also reside in [location]. Defendant is not flight risk, as all
 family connections are in [location].
 6.

 Defendant appeared at arraignment on a summons and provided the Court no reason to think any
 security is necessary for Defendant's appearance at hearings in this case.

 Application to Modify Bail (MA)

WHEREFORE, Defendant respectfully prays that the Court will inquire into this Motion and release Defendant
on personal recognizance. Alternatively, Defendant requests that if bail is required, that the Court set a
reasonable bail not exceeding [proposed bond amount (e.g., two hundred dollars ($200.00))].

Fee Agreement

 Fee Agreement (Criminal Matter) (MA)

 [firm letterhead]

 [date]

[Client's first and last name]

[Client's address]

PERSONAL AND CONFIDENTIAL

Dear [Mr./Mrs./Ms.] [Client last name]:

I appreciate the opportunity to act as your legal counsel. This letter sets forth the basic terms upon which you
have engaged our firm to represent you, including the anticipated scope of our services and the billing policies
and practices that will apply to the engagement.

Although I expect our normal method of communication will be less formal than a written statement such as
this, I believe it is important to set forth the terms of our engagement. I request that you review this letter
carefully and, if it is consistent with your understanding of our respective responsibilities, please return a signed
copy of this letter to me at your earliest convenience.

In order to avoid confusion in the future regarding the terms of my representation, I believe it will be helpful to
set forth in this letter the basic terms of my engagement. They are as follows:
 1. Scope of Engagement.

 In general, you have requested advice and representation involving the criminal allegations against you.
 Specifically, my services will include representation of you in Docket No. [number], which is pending in
 [court's name]. This agreement does not include any appeal involving Docket No. [number] or any other
 matter not listed.
 2. Billing Policies and Procedures.

 I generally charge for legal services based on the guideline hourly rates of our lawyers and other
 professionals. I will be responsible for overall supervision of the legal services provided to you by the firm.
 My guideline hourly rate is $ [dollar amount]. For this matter, I will charge a flat fee for legal services as
 follows for which you agree to pay a fee of [fee amount (e.g., Ten Thousand Dollars ($10,000)], paid on the
 date of this agreement.
 3. Out-of-Pocket Expenses.

 [Name of client] will pay all out-of-pocket expenses, including but not limited to, fees and expenses for
 private investigators, expert witnesses, court reporters, computerized research, couriers, shipping and
 postage, long distance telephone calls, fax expenses, filing fees, court costs, photocopying costs, travel
 expenses and the like. It is further agreed that any long distance phone calls made in connection with this
 case may be charged to [name of client or third party]. [Name of client] shall pay reimbursement of
 expenses within thirty (30) days of issuance of a bill.
 4. Outcome.

 It is understood that [name of law firm] has made no promises as to the outcome of this case except that
 [name of law firm] promises to render its best professional skill possible.
 5. Record Retention.

 Fee Agreement (Criminal Matter) (MA)

 At the conclusion of your case, it is my firm's usual practice to retain only certain portions of your file,
 returning and/or destroying documents not typically retained in storage. We shall allow you to retain these
 files at your discretion. If you choose not to retain said files, they will be destroyed pursuant to my firm's
 retention policy.
 6. Fee Dispute.

 You and our law firm agree that any dispute regarding this agreement shall be submitted to the Fee
 Arbitration Board of the Massachusetts Bar Association for resolution.

We look forward to working with you. Please do not hesitate to call me if you have any questions concerning
these matters.

 Fee Agreement (Criminal Matter) (MA)

 Very truly yours,
 ____________________
 [name of attorney for defendant]

 AS AGREED:
 ____________________
 [Client's first and last name]

[County], ss. [court name]

 OF THE TRIAL COURT

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

COMMONWEALTH; )

 )

 )

v. ) Docket No. [number]

 )

[name of defendant] )

 )

 Defendant. )

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

 DEFENDANT'S MOTION FOR BILL OF PARTICULARS

COMES NOW [name of defendant], Defendant herein, by and through Defendant's undersigned attorney,
and pursuant to Rule 13(b) of the Massachusetts Rules of Criminal Procedure, hereby moves this Court to
enter an Order directing the Commonwealth to file a Bill of Particulars as to the following matters
concerning the offenses charged in the Indictment herein:
PARTICULARS SOUGHT
 1.

 As used in this Motion, the term "co-conspirator", wherever it appears, includes all alleged co-
 conspirators, both those indicted as well as those unindicted or uncharged.
 2.
 (a)

 The names of all co-conspirators, presently known to the Commonwealth, and their addresses at
 the time of their alleged participation in the alleged conspiracies set out in Counts One and Two of
 the Indictment herein;
 (b)

 Any overt acts not enumerated in Counts One and Two of the Indictment, concerning which acts
 the Commonwealth intends to offer evidence upon the trial of the Indictment herein;
 (c)

 Any act done or caused to be done by this Defendant during the conspiracies alleged in Counts
 One and Two of the Indictment, which the prosecution contends was done in furtherance of the
 schemes or conspiracies alleged in Counts One and Two of the Indictment;
 (d)

 The precise time of day, place, and location where each of the overt acts of the conspiracies
 alleged in Counts One and Two of the Indictment are alleged to have been performed;
 (e)

 The particular acts of the conspiracies alleged in Counts One and Two of the Indictment, which the
 Defendant is alleged to have personally performed;
 (f)

 When, where, and in what manner each of the Defendants is alleged to have become a member of
 the conspiracies charged in Counts One and Two of the Indictment herein;
 (g)

 The particular manner in which each of these named Defendants is alleged to have aided, abetted,
 counseled, commanded, induced, procured, or willfully caused the illegal importation into the
 Commonwealth of a controlled substance by co-Defendants [names of co-Defendants], as alleged
 in Count Three of the Indictment herein, and in particular, state the nature of the acts by which it is
 claimed this named Defendant aided, abetted, counseled, commanded, induced, procured, or
 willfully caused the codefendants named hereinabove in this subparagraph to commit said offense
 and the places where such acts occurred and the dates for each such act;
 (h)

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

 The particular manner in which each of the Defendants is alleged to have illegally possessed with
 intent to distribute a controlled substance as alleged in Count Four of the Indictment herein, and in
 particular, state the nature of the acts by which it is claimed the named Defendant illegally
 possessed with intent to distribute a controlled substance and the places where such acts occurred
 and the dates for each such act;
 (i)

 The names of any persons present at or who participated in the commission of the offense alleged
 in Count Three of the Indictment, to wit: possession with intent to distribute/trafficking in violation of
 M.G.L., Ch 94C;
 (j)

 The name of the individual from whom the named Defendant, or any of the codefendants,
 allegedly received the controlled substances made the basis for the offenses alleged in Counts,
 One, Two, Three, and Four of the Indictment/Criminal Complaint herein.
 3.

 The particular manner in which any one or all of these named Defendants participated in the offense
 alleged in the aforesaid Paragraph 1. of Count One of the Indictment, to wit: conspiracy to import
 [controlled substance], and including, but not limited to, the particular manner in which the named
 Defendant committed any of the overt acts numbered (1) through ([number]) alleged to have occurred
 in furtherance of the aforesaid offense alleged in Count One of the Indictment, which overt acts form
 the gravamen of the offense.
CITATION OF AUTHORITIES
 4.

 This Motion is not an attack on the sufficiency of the Indictment/Criminal Complaint. "The fact that a
 complaint or indictment is framed in the form permitted by G.L. c. 277, s 79, and will therefore withstand
 an attack as to its sufficiency (formerly by a motion to quash, now by a motion to dismiss under G.L. c.
 277, s 47A, inserted by St.1965, c. 617, s 1) is not decisive on the question whether the court should
 exercise its discretionary power to order particulars." Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77
 (1975). The purpose of Mass. R. Civ. P. 13 is not to cure indictments or complaints, but provide the
 defense the opportunity to fairly prepare [his/her/their] defense. Id.
 5.

 The names of all co-conspirators requested in Paragraphs 2. and 3. of this Motion, who are not named
 in the Indictment but are known to the prosecution, should be provided by the Commonwealth by Bill of
 Particulars. See Commonwealth v. Nelson, 26 Mass. App. Ct. 794, 799 (1989).
 6.

 The overt acts requested in Paragraphs 3. and 4. of this Motion which are not specified in the
 Indictment but which the Government contends were committed in the furtherance of the alleged
 conspiracy and upon which the Government may rely at trial should be provided by the Government by
 Bill of Particulars. Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77 (1975); Mass. R. Crim. P 13(b).
 7.

 The precise time of day, place, and location where the overt acts of the alleged conspiracies were
 committed which are requested in Paragraph 2. of this Motion should be produced by the Government
 by Bill of Particulars, because the Defendant is entitled to be apprised of the precise time of day and
 place within a city or other area in which an offense is alleged to have occurred. Commonwealth v.

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77 (1975); Mass. Gen. Laws Ann. ch. 277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a
bill of particulars" in drug distribution cases); Mass. R. Crim. P 13(b).
8.

 The particular acts of the conspiracies alleged to have been personally performed by the named
Defendant requested in Paragraphs 2. and 3. of this Motion should be provided by the Government by
a Bill of Particulars. Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77 (1975); Mass. Gen. Laws Ann. ch. 277,
§ 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill of particulars" in drug distribution cases); Mass. R. Crim. P
13(b).
9.

 The time, date, place, and manner in which the named Defendant is alleged to have become a
member of the charged conspiracies requested in Paragraph 2. of this Motion should be provided by
the Government by a Bill of Particulars. Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77 (1975); Mass. Gen.
Laws Ann. ch. 277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill of particulars" in drug distribution cases);
Mass. R. Crim. P 13(b).
10.

 The manner in which each of the Defendants is alleged to have aided, abetted, counseled,
commanded, induced, procured or caused the commission of the offenses requested in Paragraph 2. of
this Motion, including the dates, places, and nature of the acts by which it is claimed that the Defendant
accomplished same, should be provided by the Government by Bill of Particulars. Commonwealth v.
Baker, 368 Mass. 58 (1975); Mass. Gen. Laws Ann. ch. 277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill
of particulars" in drug distribution cases); Mass. R. Crim. P 13(b).
11.

 The names of any persons present at or who participated in the commission of the offense requested
in Paragraph 2. of Defendant's Motion should be provided by the Government by Bill of Particulars.
Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77, 330 N.E.2d 794, 805 (1975); Mass. Gen. Laws Ann. ch.
277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill of particulars" in drug distribution cases); Mass. R. Crim.
P 13(b).
12.

 The name of the individual or individuals from whom the named Defendant or codefendants allegedly
received the controlled substance requested in Paragraphs 2. and 3. of this Motion should be provided
by the Government by Bill of Particulars. Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77 (1975); Mass.
Gen. Laws Ann. ch. 277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill of particulars" in drug distribution
cases); Mass. R. Crim. P 13(b).
13.

 With regard to the particulars requested in Paragraphs 2. and 3. of this Motion relating to the alleged
conspiracies, it is imperative that the Government provide the Defendant with the precise period of said
alleged conspiracies, as well as when said conspiracies began, in order to determine whether or not
certain acts or conduct fall within the applicable statute of limitations and to adequately prepare
defenses thereto; to be provided with particulars as to the names of alleged co-conspirators who
personally committed the various acts alleged therein in order to adequately prepare a defense thereto,
Commonwealth v. Baker, 368 Mass. 58, 77, 330 N.E.2d 794, 805 (1975); Mass. Gen. Laws Ann. ch.
277, § 38 ("defendant shall be entitled to a bill of particulars" in drug distribution cases); Mass. R. Crim.
P 13(b).

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

 The purpose of the bill of particular "is to give notice and guard against surprise on the trial, under the
 regulation of the court." Commonwealth v. Davis, 28 Mass. 432, 442 (1831).
SUMMARY AND CONCLUSIONS
 14.

 This Motion is not interposed for delay, but rather the matters and particulars hereinabove requested
 are essential to enable the Defendants to adequately be apprised of the nature and scope of the
 accusations against them, as guaranteed by the Sixth Amendment to the Constitution of the United
 States and, art. 12 of the Declaration of Rights of the Massachusetts Constitution to have an
 opportunity to adequately prepare their defenses, to avoid prejudicial surprise at trial, to clarify the
 issues herein and avoid confusion and delay at trial, and to enable the Defendants to be protected
 against a second prosecution for the same offense and plead double jeopardy thereto as guaranteed
 by the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution of the United States.
 15.

 The particulars requested herein are within the knowledge and control of the Government and its
 agents, and cannot be obtained by these Defendants other than by Order of this Court. The particulars
 requested herein are not privileged and compliance poses no undue burden on the Government.

WHEREFORE, premises considered, and for such other reasons as may appear to this Court at hearing,
the Defendant prays as follows:
 (a)

 That the Court order the Commonwealth to furnish a Bill of Particulars as requested in this Motion;
 (b)

 That as to any items in the Motion concerning which the Commonwealth shall state in its Bill of
 Particulars that its knowledge or information is incomplete, the Commonwealth shall set forth in its Bill
 of Particulars whatever information and knowledge it may have and shall furnish further particulars
 upon obtaining further knowledge or information prior to trial;
 (c)

 That the defendant be allowed to supplement and amend this Motion as may be necessary based on
 further discovery as provided by the Commonwealth or as may be ordered by the Court, for which
 Defendants cannot now be aware of or plan for; and
 (d)

 That the defendant be awarded such other and further relief as this Honorable Court deems just and
 proper.

 Motion for Bill of Particulars (MA)

Date: [date]
Respectfully submitted,
____________________
[name of attorney for defendant]
Attorney for Defendant

 foregoing by United States First Class Mail/hand-delivery.

 This [date] day of [month], [year].

 Motion to Dismiss for Failure to State an Offense (MA)

MOTION TO DISMISS BASED ON [basis for motion]

 Now comes Defendant [name of defendant] by their attorney, [name of attorney for defendant], and for
 this Motion to Dismiss [Indictment/Count [count number]] for Failure to State an Offense under Rule 13
 of the Rules of Criminal Procedure, states as follows.
 1.

 The [indictment/complaint] states, in pertinent part: [count at issue].
 2.

 An [indictment/complaint] must allege every essential element of the offense. Harris v. United
 States, 536 U.S. 545, 549, 122 S. Ct. 2406, 2410, 153 L. Ed. 2d 524, 532 (2002) ("In federal
 prosecutions, 'no person shall be held to answer for a capital, or otherwise infamous crime, unless
 on a presentment or indictment of a Grand Jury' alleging all the elements of the crime.") (quoting
 U.S. Const. amend. V); Castillo v. United States, 530 U.S. 120, 123, 120 S. Ct. 2090, 2092, 147 L.
 Ed. 2d 94, 98 (2000) (if fact is element, "indictment must identify" it); Commonwealth v. Geagan,
 339 Mass. 487, 495 (1959) (A motion to quash is confined to taking objection to an indictment 'for a
 formal defect apparent on the face thereof.") The charge of assault and battery requires proof the
 defendant intentionally touched the complainant without the complainant's consent. Commonwealth
 v. Colon, 81 Mass. App. Ct. 8 (2011). Here, the record reflects the complainant consented to
 whatever touching occurred.
 3.

 The [indictment/complaint] fails to allege the element of [name element] [case citation of case
 finding element essential], which is an essential element of the offense of [offense and statute
 citation]. Since the [indictment/complaint] omits an essential element, it fails to charge an offense.

 PROSECUTION'S REQUEST FOR DISCOVERY

 NOW COMES the Commonwealth, by and through the undersigned district attorney, and hereby moves
 this Court pursuant to Massachusetts Rule of Criminal Procedure 14.1 for an order requiring the Defendant
 to provide reciprocal discovery to the Commonwealth as follows:
 1.

 An opportunity to inspect and copy or photograph books, papers, documents, photographs, motion
 pictures, mechanical or electronic recordings, tangible objects, or copies or portions thereof which are
 within the possession, custody, or control of the Defendant and which the Defendant intends to
 introduce in evidence at the trial.
 2.

 An opportunity to inspect and copy or photograph results or reports of physical or mental examinations
 or of tests, measurements or experiments made in connection with the case, or copies thereof, within
 the possession and control of the Defendant which the Defendant intends to introduce in evidence at
 trial or which were prepared by an expert witness whom the Defendant intends to call at trial, when the
 results or reports relate to [his/her/their] testimony. In addition, upon motion of the Commonwealth, the
 Court must order the Defendant to permit the Prosecution to inspect, examine, and test, subject to
 appropriate safeguards, any physical evidence or a sample of it available to the Defendant if the
 Defendant intends to offer such evidence, or tests or experiments made in connection with such
 evidence, as an exhibit or evidence in the case.
 3.

 Notice of the intent to offer at trial a defense of alibi, duress, entrapment, insanity, mental infirmity,
 diminished capacity, self-defense, accident, automatism, involuntary intoxication, or voluntary
 intoxication.
 4.

 Notice of any expert witnesses that the Defendant reasonably expects to call as a witness at trial. Each
 such witness shall prepare, and the Defendant shall furnish to the Prosecution, a report on the results
 of the examinations or tests conducted by the expert. The Defendant shall also furnish to the
 Prosecution the expert's curriculum vitae, the expert's opinion, and the underlying basis for that opinion.

 Motion to Revise and/or Revoke Sentence (MA)

 MOTION TO REVISE AND REVOKE SENTENCE

Comes now the defendant, [name of defendant], by counsel, and moves this Court, pursuant to Rule 29(a)
of the Mass. R. Crim. P., to modify the defendant's [length of sentence (e.g., fifteen-year)] sentence
imposed by the jury on [month day, year] for [name of offense] under [applicable statute] and to fix a
maximum term of imprisonment for [length of sentence]-the minimum sentence authorized for this charge.
The reasons for this motion are delineated below.
1.

This motion is timely, as the Court imposed the sentence less than 60 days ago. Mass. R. Crim. P. 29.
2.

 When sentence of imprisonment for a felony is fixed by a trial judge, having regard to the nature and
circumstances of the crime and to the history and character of the defendant, is of the opinion that a
sentence of imprisonment is necessary but that the maximum term fixed by the Court is unduly harsh, the
Court may modify that sentence and fix a maximum term within the limits provided in [applicable statute] for
the offense for which the defendant presently stands convicted.
3.

 On [month day, year], the jury convicted the defendant of [name of offense]-under [applicable statute].
The authorized maximum term of imprisonment for [name of offense] is not less than [length of minimum
sentence] nor more than [length of maximum sentence]. [citation to relevant statute.] The Court sentenced
the defendant to [length of sentence] imprisonment.
4.

 [Provide reasons that support modification of the defendant's sentence length. Add as many sections as
necessary to provide sufficient support for the motion.] See attached Affidavit of [name of defendant].
5.

 In view of the above, this Court should regard the jury's [length of sentence] sentence as "unjust" and
modify the sentence to the statutory minimum sentence for this offense. [cite to statute]. A more culpable
co-defendant was sentenced to the minimum sentence subsequently to the imposition of the sentence here
and that is a proper ground to find this sentence unjust. Commonwealth v. Tejeda, 481 Mass. 794, 796–97
(2019).

 Motion to Revise and/or Revoke Sentence (MA)

WHEREFORE this Court should grant this motion and, pursuant to [statute], modify the defendant's [length of
sentence] sentence previously imposed by the jury by fixing the maximum term of imprisonment at [length of
minimum sentence]-the minimum sentence authorized under for [name of charge].
Respectfully submitted,

 MOTION TO REVISE AND/OR REVOKE SENTENCE ON THE GROUNDS IT WAS
 [UNAUTHORIZED/ILLEGALLY IMPOSED/ INVALID AS A MATTER OF LAW]

Comes now the defendant, [name of defendant], by counsel, and moves this Court, pursuant to Rule 29(a) of
the Mass. R. Crim. P., to revoke the defendant's [length of sentence (e.g., fifteen-year)] sentence imposed by
the jury on [month] [day], [year] for the of [offense] under [statute] and to fix a maximum term of imprisonment
for [length of time]-the minimum sentence authorized under the for this charge for the following reasons:
 1.

 This motion is timely, as the Court imposed the sentence less than sixty days ago. Mass. R. Crim. P. 29.
 2.

 "[W]here the sentencing disposition of the criminal case is claimed to be illegal, whether it be a conviction,
 straight probation, or a continuance without a finding, it is subject to challenge pursuant to a rule 29 motion
 to revise or revoke." Commonwealth v. Beverly, 485 Mass. 1, 10, 147 N.E.3d 426, 434 (2020);
 Commonwealth v. Rossetti, 485 Mass. 24, 27, 146 N.E.3d 1128, 1132 (2020).
 3.

 Here, the Court imposed a jail term when none was authorized under the law [cite statute under which
 sentenced], rendering this sentence an illegal and it must be vacated.

WHEREFORE this Court should grant this motion and vacate the defendant's sentence.

 Pursuant to Mass. R. App. P. 27.1, Appellant [appellant name] (hereafter "Appellant") respectfully
 requests that this Honorable Court grant further appellate review of the Appeals Court's opinion issued in
 this case on [month] [day], [year]. See [citation of appeals court's decision] (attached as Ex. A). As grounds
 hereto, the Appellant states that further appellate review is necessitated by substantial reasons affecting
 the public interest and the interests of justice, as discussed below.
II. STATEMENT OF PRIOR PROCEEDINGS.
 On [month] [day], [year], the Appellant was indicted for the offense of [offense name], a
 [felony/misdemeanor] under [statutory citation]. The Appellant entered a plea of not guilty to [this/these]
 [offense/offenses] and the matter was scheduled for a jury trial on [month] [day], [year]. After the trial, the
 Appellant was found guilty of the charged [offense/offenses] and received a sentence of [length/terms of
 sentence] [months/years].
 The Appellant filed an appeal of the Superior Court's decision on [month] [day], [year]. [His/Her/Their]
 Appeal was entered with the Appeals Court on [month] [day], [year]. The Appellant and Commonwealth
 filed opposing briefs and presented oral arguments on [month] [day], [year]. The Appeals Court then issued
 its decision on [month] [day], [year] and affirmed the Superior Court's decision. The Appellant is seeking
 reconsideration of that decision.
III. STATEMENT OF FACTS.
 [Provide the court with a concise, but detailed factual background for your case]
IV. POINTS TO WHICH FURTHER APPELLATE REVIEW OF THE DECISION OF THE APPEALS COURT IS
SOUGHT.
 Whether the Appeals Court erred in affirming the Superior Court's decision convicting the Appellant
 [provide basis of argument (e.g., without a fair trial or sufficient evidence].
V. REASONS FOR FURTHER APPELLATE REVIEW.
 The Appellant was convicted without a fair trial or sufficient evidence. The Massachusetts Appeals Court
 has failed to conform to settled law. If allowed to stand, this opinion will affect an untold number of future
 criminal cases in the Commonwealth by allowing trials by biased juries and convictions to stand even
 though the Commonwealth fails to meet its burden and prove defendants' guilt beyond a reasonable doubt.
 This Court should exercise its discretion to review this case because under Mass. R. App. P. 27.1(a), these
 are substantial reasons affecting the public interest and the interests of justice.

 CONCLUSION

 The Appellant respectfully requests further appellate review of the Massachusetts Appeals Court's decision
 in this case. This case raises important issues of law and public interest related to fair jury trials and
 sufficiency of evidence.

imprisonment upon the ground that said sentence [was illegally imposed/[describe other ground]] and said
Motion having been heard on [month] [day], [year], and having read the affirmation of defense counsel dated
[month] [day], [year], in support of the Motion and the affirmation of [assistant commonwealth attorney name],
attorney for the Commonwealth, in opposition, and the moving papers and [exhibit/exhibits] annexed thereto
having alleged a ground which constitutes legal basis for the motion, and the allegations of fact being
substantiated by unquestionable documentary proof, to wit, the certified copy of the [month] [day], [year],

the necessity of conducting a hearing and said Motion having come on to be heard on [month] [day], [year], and
after hearing the Defendant's attorney for the motion and the attorney for the Commonwealth, in opposition, and
due deliberation having been had thereon, I decide and find as follows:
 FINDINGS OF FACT

 [he/she/they] [was/were] found guilty of the said offense of [offense name(s)] on [month] [day], [year].

ground that it was obtained in violation of [his/her/their] constitutional right to due process and said Motion
having come to be heard on [month] [day], [year], and having read the affirmation of the Defendant's attorney,
[defendant attorney name], sworn to [month] [day], [year], and the affidavit of, the trial witness, sworn to [month]

Commonwealth, opposed;

And the moving papers and exhibits annexed thereto having alleged a ground constituting a legal basis for the
Motion, and such ground being supported by sworn allegations of the existence of facts, and said sworn
allegations of fact having been substantiated by unquestionable documentary proof, to wit the certified copy of
the [month] [day], [year], stenographic minutes of trial, and upon considering the merits of the said Motion
without the necessity of conducting a hearing, and said Motion having come to be heard on [month] [day],
[year], and after hearing the Defendant's attorney for the Motion, and the attorney for the Commonwealth,
opposed, and due deliberation having been had thereon, I decide and find as follows:
 FINDINGS OF FACT
 1.

 The Defendant was indicted by the [county] County Grand Jury for [offense name] in that [he/she/they]
 allegedly did [provide facts listed in indictment].
 2.

 In the trial of this case on [month] [day], [year], [witness name] testified as the Commonwealth's
 principal witness.
 3.

 During [his/her/their] testimony, [assistant district attorney name], attorney for the Commonwealth,
 asked [him/her/them] about [his/her/their] impression of [prior witness name], another witness the
 Commonwealth called beforehand.
 4.

 This fact is supported by [witness name] affidavit as well as the stenographic record of [his/her/their]
 testimony.
 CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
 1.

 This line of questioning by the Commonwealth constitutes misconduct as [he/she/they] are not
 permitted to elicit a witness' opinion of another witness' testimony. See United States v. Geston, 299
 F.3d 1130 (9th Cir. 2002).
 2.

 The judgment of conviction dated [month] [day], [year], deprived the Defendant of [his/her/their] liberty
 without due process of law.
 3.

 The Defendant is entitled to an order vacating the [month] [day], [year], judgment of conviction and
 directing a new trial of the indictment.

THEREFORE, upon Defendant's Notice of Motion, dated [month] [day], [year], to vacate the [month] [day],

 RE: [case name]

 App. Div. Docket No.: [year] [number]

 Dear: [Defendant name]:

 As your assigned appellate counsel, I have carefully reviewed the record of the proceedings of your case in the
 trial court for the purpose of preparing a brief for you on appeal. The result of that review is that I have been
 unable to find any non-frivolous issues that can be raised on your behalf. Accordingly, I am filing the enclosed
 brief with the Appeals Court pursuant to the cases of Anders v. California, 386 U.S. 738 (1967) and
 Commonwealth v. Moffett, 383 Mass. 201 (1981). In this brief I have asked to be relieved as your attorney
 because I could not find a non-frivolous issue.

 If the Court accepts my analysis, it will grant my motion to be relieved from representing you and will affirm the
 [judgment of conviction/Order] from which you appealed. It is very important, therefore, that you be aware that
 you have the right to file a pro se supplemental brief with the Appeals Court setting forth any points that you
 think ought to be raised on your appeal. The Court will conduct its own review of the record and any
 supplemental brief from you, and if it concludes that a non-frivolous ground exists for reversal or modification of
 the [judgment/Order], it will assign new appellate counsel to represent you.

 If you wish to file a pro se supplemental brief, you must simply ask for permission to do so by writing a letter to
 the Appeals Court.

 Yours truly,
 ____________________
 [Attorney name]

Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing

Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS
 [COUNTY], SS.
 [COURT NAME] OF THE TRIAL COURT

 Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

COMMONWEALTH; )

 ) Docket No. [number]

v. )

[defendant name] )

Defendant. )

 Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

 This memorandum of law is respectfully submitted in support of a Motion, dated [month] [day], [year],
 whereby the Defendant seeks an Order, pursuant to Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 278A, allowing
 [him/her/them] to obtain post-conviction DNA testing of evidence and granting such other and further relief
 as to the Court deems just and proper.

 Section 2 of Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 278A provides that, "A person may file a motion for
 forensic or scientific analysis under this chapter if that person: (1) has been convicted of a criminal offense
 in a court of the commonwealth; (2) is incarcerated in a state prison, house of correction, is on parole or
 probation or whose liberty has been otherwise restrained as the result of a conviction; and (3) asserts
 factual innocence of the crime for which the person has been convicted."

 [Defendant name] was convicted of [offense names, (e.g., rape)] and [type of evidence (e.g., a sexual
 assault kit)] was collected, which undoubtedly contained the DNA of the perpetrator. With the availability of
 new types of DNA analysis that will be described herein, more advanced testing is now possible. If the
 results of DNA testing of this at-issue evidence are favorable, their admission at trial would create a
 reasonable probability that the Defendant would have received a more favorable verdict. Accordingly, this
 Court should grant the relief requested in the underlying Motion.
STATEMENT OF FACTS

 The facts of this case, insofar as pertinent to the underlying Motion, are contained in the accompanying
 affirmation of [name of defendant's attorney] duly affirmed on the [day] day of [month], [year], and the
 exhibits appended thereto, all of which are incorporated herein and made a part hereof.
ARGUMENT

 THIS COURT SHOULD ORDER THE EVIDENCE USED AT TRIAL TO CONVICT THE DEFENDANT TO
 UNDERGO DNA TESTING PURSUANT TO G.L. C. 278A, § 2.
 1.

 The Defendant has satisfied the three requirements set forth in G.L. C. 278A, § 2 and is
 therefore entitled to obtain DNA testing of the at-issue evidence.

 First, the Defendant was convicted of [identify offense(s)] after a trial at [court name], a court in the
 Commonwealth. Further, the Defendant is currently [incarcerated in a state prison or house of
 corrections/on parole or probation]. Finally, since the instigation of this case to the present day, the
 Defendant has maintained [his/her/their] innocence of the [offense/offenses] of which [he/she/they]
 [was/were] convicted. Based on the satisfaction of these three requirements, the Defendant is entitled
 to have the [identify evidence you are asking to be tested (e.g., sexual assault kit)] undergo testing for
 DNA.
 2.

 The analysis of the evidence in this case using current Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)
 would be admissible in courts in the Commonwealth and will provide an accurate identification
 of the perpetrator of the underlying [offense/offenses] of this case.

 A PCR (polymerase chain reaction) test is a way to look for genetic material (DNA or RNA). After taking
 a body fluid sample (like blood) or a swab from a body site (like deep in your nose), scientists use PCR
 to make many copies of DNA (amplification) that was in the original sample. By amplifying with PCR,
 scientists can better analyze the DNA or RNA that was in the original sample. See Cleveland Clinic,
 PCR Test. As this is the current analysis used to test DNA, if it is relevant and administered by a
 qualified expert, it is admissible in courts in the Commonwealth.

 Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

 [Provide specific details supporting this argument.] In this case, [type of evidence collected or asking to
 be tested (e.g., sexual assault kit)] was collected and analyzed using the rudimentary technology
 available at the time of trial. Since then, DNA analysis has evolved and the current PCR analysis will
 provide an accurate picture of the perpetrator's DNA that was collected. Based on this, the Court
 should allow the Defendant to have this evidence undergo this advanced testing.
CONCLUSION

 For the foregoing reasons, the Defendant respectfully requests that this Court grant [his/her/their] Motion to
 obtain post-conviction DNA testing of the above-identified evidence and for such other relief the Court
 deems just and proper.

 Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

Respectfully submitted,
____________________
(Signature of Defendant's attorney)

 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS

 Memorandum of Law in Support of Motion for Writ of Error Coram Nobis (MA)

PRELIMINARY STATEMENT

 This memorandum of law is respectfully submitted in support of a Motion, dated [month] [day], [year],
 whereby the Defendant seeks an Order, pursuant to Massachusetts Rule of Criminal Procedure 30,
 vacating [his/her/their] judgment based on newly discovered evidence and granting such other and further
 relief as to the Court deems just and proper.

 Subsection (a) of the Rule provides, "Any person who is imprisoned or whose liberty is restrained pursuant
 to a criminal conviction may at any time, as of right, file a written motion requesting the trial judge to release
 him or her or to correct the sentence then being served upon the ground that the confinement or restraint
 was imposed in violation of the Constitution or laws of the United States or of the Commonwealth of
 Massachusetts."

 [Defendant name] was convicted of [offense name(s)] and received a sentence of [length/terms of
 sentence] [months/year]. However, [identify new facts that were unknown to court at time judgment was
 rendered (e.g., the fact that the Defendant was not informed by counsel that it was his, her, or their decision
 whether to testify on their own behalf)]. Therefore, the sentence the Defendant received resulted from a
 violation of [his/her/their] constitutional rights and should therefore be vacated.
STATEMENT OF FACTS

 The facts of this case, insofar as pertinent to the underlying Motion, are contained in the accompanying
 affirmation of [defendant attorney name] duly affirmed on the [day] day of [month], [year], and the exhibits
 appended thereto, all of which are incorporated herein and made a part hereof.
ARGUMENT

 THIS COURT SHOULD VACATE THE JUDGMENT ENTERED AGAINST THE DEFENDANT BECAUSE
 IT RESULTED FROM A CONVICTION OBTAINED IN VIOLATION OF [HIS/HER/THEIR]
 CONSTITUTIONAL RIGHTS.
 1.

 The judgment in the Defendant's case should be vacated pursuant to Massachusetts Rule of
 Criminal Procedure 30(a).

 The Defendant was convicted of [name offense(s)] after a jury trial and received a sentence of [length of
 sentence] [months/years]. During this trial, the Defendant informed the Court that [he/she/they] did not wish
 to testify. Unknown to the trial Court, and outside of the record, is the fact that Defendant's trial counsel
 failed to inform the Defendant that it was [his/her/their] decision as to whether or not to testify. More
 specifically, Defendant's trial counsel led the Defendant to believe that it was counsel's decision as to
 whether the Defendant testified. The Defendant, like all criminal defendants, has a constitutional right to
 effective assistance of counsel. See Strickland v. Washington, 466 U.S. 668 (1984). Based on these newly
 discovered facts, this right was violated in the Defendant's case which warrants the vacation of
 [his/her/their] judgment pursuant to Massachusetts Rule of Criminal Procedure 30(a).
CONCLUSION

 For the foregoing reasons, the Defendant respectfully requests that this Court grant [his/her/their] Motion for
 Writ of Error Coram Nobis, vacate [his/her/their] judgment, and for such other relief the Court deems just
 and proper.

 Notice of Motion for Post-Conviction DNA Testing (MA)

TAKE NOTICE that upon the attached affidavit of [defendant attorney name], attorney for the Defendant, sworn
to on [month] [day], [year], the attached exhibits, the accompanying memorandum of law, and all prior
proceedings had to date, the undersigned will move this Court for an order (1) to ascertain whether evidence
containing DNA collected at or about the time of the crime still exists and (2) to determine the specific location
where these items are located, so that (3) DNA testing may be obtained by the Defendant because if the results
of DNA testing of that evidence had been admitted at trial, there exists a reasonable probability that the
Defendant would have received a more favorable verdict, and for such other further relief as the Court may
deem just and proper. Said hearing will be held at the [county name] County Courthouse at [street address],
[city], Massachusetts, on the [day] of [month], [year], at [time] [AM/PM] or as soon thereafter as the undersigned

[Defendant attorney name], an attorney admitted to practice in the courts of the Commonwealth of
Massachusetts, hereby affirms the following under penalty of perjury:
 1.

 I am familiar with the facts and proceedings herein. I make this affirmation in support of the Defendant's
 Motion for an Order granting reconsideration of this Court's Order dated [day] day of [month], [year],
 affirming on appeal a judgment rendered in the [court] Court, [county] County, on the [day] day of [month],
 [year], convicting [him/her/them] of and sentencing [him/her/them] thereon.
 2.

 The Defendant was indicted on [month] [day], [year], and was charged with the commission of [offense
 name], a [class of felony] felony.
 3.

 The Defendant entered a plea of not guilty to the indictment on [month] [day], [year], and the case was
 scheduled for trial on [month] [day], [year].
 4.

 After the trial before a jury, the Defendant was found guilty of the [offense name], a class [class of felony]
 felony and an Order was entered sentencing the Defendant to [length/terms of sentence].
 5.

 Following this Order, the Defendant appealed this case to the Massachusetts Appeals Court.
 6.

 The Massachusetts Appeals Court entered an Order affirming the trial court's judgment convicting the
 Defendant.
 7.

 With due respect, the conclusions by this Honorable Court are erroneous in that [state reason(s) you are
 asking the court to reconsider its order (e.g., newly discovered evidence, error of law/fact)].

WHEREFORE, it is respectfully requested that the Defendant's Motion for Reconsideration be granted and for
such other relief as the Court deems just and proper.

[Defendant attorney name], an attorney duly admitted to practice law in the courts of the Commonwealth, does

 1.

 6.

 Notice of Motion to Dismiss People's Appeal and Affirmation in Support (MA)

[Defendant attorney name], an attorney admitted to practice in the courts of the Commonwealth of
Massachusetts, hereby affirms the following under penalty of perjury:
 1.

 I am familiar with the facts and proceedings herein. I make this affirmation in support of the Motion to
 Dismiss the Commonwealth's appeal from a judgment rendered in the [court] Court, [county] County, on the
 [day] day of [month], [year], dismissing the [charge/charges] against the Defendant.
 2.

 The Defendant was indicted on [month] [day], [year], and was charged with the commission of [offense
 name], a [class of felony] felony.
 3.

 The Defendant entered a plea of not guilty to the indictment on [month] [day], [year], and the case was
 scheduled for trial on [month] [day], [year].
 4.

 After the trial before a jury, the Defendant was found not guilty of the [offense name], a class [class of
 felony] felony and an Order was entered dismissing the case.
 5.

 Following this Order, the Commonwealth appealed this case to the Massachusetts Appeals Court.
 6.

 This appeal, as argued in the principal Motion should be dismissed because [identify reason(s) you are
 asking the court to dismiss the Commonwealth's appeal (e.g., the appeal does not involve a proper legal
 issue and the trial court's decision was not clearly erroneous].

WHEREFORE, it is respectfully requested that the Defendant's Motion to Dismiss the Commonwealth's
pending appeal be granted and for such other relief as the Court deems just and proper.

Date: ____________________
Respectfully submitted,
____________________
(Signature of Defendant's attorney)
[defendant attorney name], Attorney for Defendant
[office street address]
[OPTIONAL LANGUAGE: P.O. Box address]
[city], [state] [zip code]
Email: [email address]

[believe/believes] them to be true.

Date: ____________________

____________________

Order Setting Aside Sentence on the People's Motion Upon Ground It Was
 Invalid as a Matter of Law

Order Setting Aside Sentence on the People's Motion Upon Ground It Was Invalid as a Matter of Law (MA)

 COMMONWEALTH OF MASSACHUSETTS
 [COUNTY], SS.
 [COURT NAME] OF THE TRIAL COURT

 Order Setting Aside Sentence on the People's Motion Upon Ground It Was Invalid as a Matter of Law (MA)

COMMONWEALTH; )

 )

 ) Docket No. [number]

v. )

 )

[defendant name] )

 )

Defendant. )

Order Setting Aside Sentence on the People's Motion Upon Ground It Was Invalid as a Matter of Law (MA)

The Commonwealths having moved this Court to set aside the Defendant's, sentence of imprisonment upon the
ground that said sentence [was illegally imposed/[describe other ground]] and said Motion having been heard
on [month] [day], [year], and having read the affirmation of [Commonwealth attorney name], the attorney for the
Commonwealth dated [month] [day], [year], in support of the Motion and the affirmation of [defendant attorney
name], attorney for the Defendant, in [support/opposition], and the moving papers and [exhibit/exhibits]
annexed thereto having alleged a ground which constitutes legal basis for the motion, and the allegations of
fact being substantiated by unquestionable documentary proof, to wit, the certified copy of the [month] [day],
[year], stenographic minutes of the sentence proceeding, and upon considering the merits of the said Motion
without the necessity of conducting a hearing and said Motion having come on to be heard on [month] [day],
[year], and after hearing the Commonwealth attorney's for the motion and the attorney for the Defendant, in
[support/opposition], and due deliberation having been had thereon, I decide and find as follows:
 FINDINGS OF FACT
 1.

 That the Defendant was indicted for the class [class of felony] felony on [month] [day], [year], and that
 [he/she/they] [was/were] found guilty of the said offense of [offense name(s)] on [month] [day], [year].
 2.

 That [he/she/they] [was/were] sentenced to a sentence of imprisonment of [length of sentence]
 [months/years] by Honorable [judge name] on [month] [day], [year].
 3.

 That the stenographic minutes of the sentencing proceedings indicate that Honorable [judge name]
 imposed this sentence using the Defendant's incorrect criminal history level leading [him/her/them] to
 impose a sentence disproportionate to the circumstances of the case.
 CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
 1.

 The [month] [day], [year], sentence was illegally imposed in that the sentencing court failed to
 accurately consider the Defendant's accurate criminal history level.

That the Defendant is entitled to an order setting aside the [month] [day], [year], sentence.

THEREFORE, upon the Commonwealth's Notice of Motion, dated [month] [day], [year], to set aside the [month]
[day], [year], sentence upon the ground that it [was unauthorized/was illegally imposed/[provide other reason
why invalid as a matter of law]] and upon the supporting affirmation of the attorney for the Commonwealth
dated [month] [day], [year], and the [supporting/opposing] affirmation of the Defendant's attorney, sworn to
[month] [day], [year], and upon the certified copy of the stenographic minutes of the [month] [day], [year],
sentence proceeding, and upon the Court's written decision filed on [month] [day], [year], it is Ordered that:
 1.

 The Defendant's motion to set aside [his/her/their] sentence is granted.
 2.

 The illegally imposed sentence of imprisonment pronounced by Honorable [judge name] is set aside.
 3.

 The Defendant is remanded to [title of appropriate sentencing court] Court of [county] County for
 resentencing according to law.

 Order Setting Aside Sentence on the People's Motion Upon Ground It Was Invalid as a Matter of Law (MA)

 Date: ____________________
 ____________________
 (Signature of judge)
